channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Pakistan Foreign Minister Expresses Concern Over Attacks from Afghan Soil
item.description: Pakistan's foreign minister, Ishaq Dar, voiced concerns about ongoing militant attacks against Pakistan originating from Afghan territory. He discussed the issue with ASEAN's secretary-general in Islamabad. Meanwhile, the Pakistan Army Chief visited the border region, reaffirming commitment to counter-terrorism efforts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Reports 29 Births Per 1,000 Girls Aged 15-19
item.description: Kyrgyzstan records 29 births per 1,000 girls aged 15-19, according to the UN Population Fund's 2026 'State of World Population' report. This rate is higher than the regional average in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. The report also details women's autonomy and family dynamics across the region.

item.title: Uzbek President Orders "Zero Waste" Principle for Granite and Marble Quarries
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has mandated that Uzbekistan's granite and marble quarries adopt a "zero waste" principle. This directive aims to increase the processing of raw material remnants into high-value products, with new projects totaling at least $100 million to be launched.

item.title: Mother of Convicted Man Appeals to President for House Arrest
item.description: The mother of Baktybek Moldaliev, sentenced to three years for distributing extremist materials, has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov for his transfer to house arrest. She stated her son is the sole breadwinner and his imprisonment has caused severe financial hardship for his family.

item.title: Almaty Hospitals Overwhelmed by Surge in Respiratory Infections
item.description: Almaty's hospitals are experiencing a significant increase in bed occupancy due to a seasonal rise in ARVI and flu cases. Residents report long queues at emergency rooms, with up to 50 people waiting for medical attention. The city's health department confirmed an increase in pediatric beds.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Discuss Resuming Direct Flights and Partial Visa-Free Travel
item.description: Uzbekistan's Deputy Foreign Minister met with the Turkmen Ambassador to discuss bilateral cooperation, including the resumption of direct flights between Tashkent and Ashgabat. They also reviewed visa-free travel arrangements for residents of border regions, based on a 2004 agreement. Specific launch dates were not announced.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Internet Surveillance Concerns and Espionage Conviction Highlighted
item.description: Kazakhstan's move to route mobile internet traffic through state-controlled nodes raises privacy concerns. Meanwhile, an Uzbekistani professor was sentenced to 10 years for espionage after a closed-door trial. Officials dismissed press freedom rating concerns as 'alarmism,' despite low rankings.

item.title: Astana Hosts "People's Lawyer" Event for Legal Assistance
item.description: Astana held the "People's Lawyer" event, offering legal aid to residents. Over thirty experts, including officials, judges, and lawyers, provided consultations for three hours. Organized by the Astana Prosecutor's Office and Akimat, the event aimed to foster direct dialogue between citizens and government officials.

item.title: Freedom Bank and 'Daryn' Center Sign Agreement to Support Talented Youth
item.description: Freedom Bank and the Republican Scientific-Practical Center 'Daryn' have signed a cooperation agreement to support gifted schoolchildren. The bank will sponsor six major national Olympiads, providing cash prizes for winners and their teachers. The first joint project supported around 200 winners of an Olympiad for rural school students.

item.title: Pension Under Construction at Bishkek Center for Protection of Mother and Child
item.description: A pension is being built on the grounds of the National Center for the Protection of Mother and Child in Bishkek for parents of children with oncological diseases. The facility will accommodate 70 people and aims to create comfortable living and rest conditions. Construction is funded by the President's Stabilization Fund.

item.title: Kyrgyzaltyn Company Reports Over 90 Billion Som Net Profit in Five Years
item.description: Kyrgyzaltyn, a state-owned gold mining company, reported a net profit exceeding 90 billion som and total revenue of 99 billion som over the past five years. The company paid 6.8 billion som in taxes to the state budget and 662 million som to the Social Fund during this period.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets November 29 for Snap Local Maslikhat Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan will hold snap elections for its local representative bodies, maslikhats, on November 29. President Tokayev called the elections after the merger of the Amanat party into a new organization, Adilet. A total of 3,447 deputies will be elected to 228 maslikhats, with 35.8 billion tenge allocated for the organization.

item.title: Uzbekistan Secures Water Supply for Under-Construction Nuclear Power Plant
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to use the South Mirzachol canal to supply water for the nuclear power plant being built in the Forish district of Jizzakh region. Water resources minister Shavkat Khamrayev stated the issue is fully resolved, emphasizing the plant's low water demand and potential for water recycling. Other water sources are also available in the area.

item.title: Kazakh President Warns Officials Against Negligence and Corruption
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized that high positions entail great responsibility. He stated that individuals making decisions affecting citizens' lives must be impeccable. Tokayev warned that those negligent in their duties will be dismissed, and criminals will face punishment, particularly concerning the 'People's Construction' program.

item.title: Kazakhstan Explores Railway Routes Through Afghanistan to Pakistan Ports
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering railway routes via Afghanistan to Pakistani seaports, with one private proposal costing $4.1 billion and aiming for a 2029 launch. This Central Asia–South Asia Railway (CASA) project aims to diversify export routes and provide direct access to South Asian markets.

item.title: Kazakhstan Needs Unified Investment Tools for Agricultural Sector
item.description: Kazakhstan should develop a unified set of investment instruments specifically tailored for its agricultural sector. This initiative aims to streamline and enhance financial support for agricultural development within the country.

item.title: Kyrgyzaltyn Company Reports Five Years of Key Achievements and Expansion
item.description: Over the past five years, Kyrgyzaltyn has transformed into a multi-sectoral holding, expanding beyond gold production. The company reported net profit exceeding 90 billion soms and total revenue surpassing 99 billion soms. Strategic mineral deposits have been brought under state control, with subsidiaries like Kumtor Gold Company developing their own production.

item.title: Emirates Considers Launching Regular Flights to Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan Airports representatives held talks with Emirates Group officials regarding the potential launch of regular flights. Emirates is considering the possibility after studying passenger demand, airport infrastructure, and commercial viability. Currently, Flydubai, Air Arabia, and Etihad Airways operate flights to Uzbekistan from the UAE.

item.title: Emirates Considers Launching Flights to Uzbekistan After Market Study
item.description: Emirates airline is exploring the possibility of launching flights to Uzbekistan. Representatives from Emirates Group met with Uzbekistan Airports to discuss entry into the local aviation market. The airline will consider flights after assessing passenger demand, airport infrastructure, and commercial potential.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Calls for Unified Investment Tools for Agriculture Sector
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed the government to develop a unified set of investment instruments for Kazakhstan's agricultural sector by the end of the first quarter of 2027. He criticized current tools for lengthy procedures and insufficient digitalization, urging increased bank participation and accessible, long-term financing tailored to agricultural cycles.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: AI-95 Gasoline Prices Not State-Regulated, Says Antimonopoly Service
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, retail prices for AI-95 gasoline are set by fuel suppliers and sellers, not by state limits, according to the State Antimonopoly Service. While temporary state regulation applies to AI-92 gasoline, diesel, and LPG, AI-95 is excluded. The service continues to monitor AI-95 prices despite the lack of a price ceiling.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish Special Zone for Nuclear Power Plant Construction Materials
item.description: Uzbekistan will open a 200-hectare special industrial zone in the Jizzakh region to produce materials for its nuclear power plant construction. The project aims to localize the production of 70 new product types, requiring an estimated $2.2 billion in construction materials. The zone will offer preferential tax and customs conditions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates 1.3 Trillion Tenge for "Children of Kazakhstan" Concept
item.description: Kazakhstan has allocated 1.3 trillion tenge for the "Children of Kazakhstan" Concept for 2026-2030. The concept, approved in January 2026, covers child safety, education, healthcare, and psychological support. The Ministry of Education reported that 70% of planned measures for 2026 have been completed.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Speaker Raises Key Initiatives at CIS Parliamentary Assembly Meeting
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, attended the 61st plenary session of the CIS Parliamentary Assembly in Turkmenistan. He delivered a report with proposals and shared initiatives to enhance relations. Mamataliev emphasized the Assembly's role in strengthening inter-state ties and parliamentary cooperation, and the need to expand economic ties among CIS member states.

item.title: Over 62% of Uzbek Teachers Failed Professional Certification Exams in Three Years
item.description: In Uzbekistan, 62.3% of teachers who took professional certification exams between 2024 and 2026 failed to obtain certification. Out of 47,936 participating teachers, 29,857 did not pass, yet 24,987 continue to work in educational institutions. The pass rate decreased slightly over the three-year period.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Offer $200 Million in Loans for New Tashkent Construction Using Local Materials
item.description: Uzbekistan will launch a $200 million credit line for developers in New Tashkent, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced. The funds are intended for working capital and will be disbursed exclusively for the purchase of local construction materials. This initiative aims to boost local production and competitiveness.

item.title: Kazakh President Emphasizes Modernizing Veterinary Sector for Export Growth
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted the need to modernize the veterinary sector during the third forum for agricultural workers. He noted that Kazakhstan has been recognized as foot-and-mouth disease-free, opening new export opportunities for meat and other livestock products. Improving livestock accounting and laboratory diagnostics is crucial.

item.title: Uzbek President Criticizes High Construction Material Imports, Promotes Local Industry
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev criticized Uzbekistan's high import volumes of construction materials while highlighting the success of local production in the "Oltin bel" tourist complex. He stressed the need for synergy between the construction and tourism sectors, emphasizing the use of domestic materials and innovative technologies to reduce costs and boost local industry.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates 150 Billion Tenge for Rural Development Program 'Aul Amanaty'
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced that 150 billion tenge has been allocated for the 'Aul Amanaty' program, which has helped employ over 22,000 rural residents. He emphasized the need for rural entrepreneurs to access digital marketplaces, banking, and logistics services. The program aims to scale up and ensure the sustainability of rural employment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Labor Minister Addresses Citizen Concerns on Disability Assistance, Employment, and Quotas
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration, Almaz Imaniaziev, held a reception for 10 citizens. Key issues raised included personal assistants for people with disabilities, employment opportunities, financial aid, and foreign worker quotas. The ministry is reviewing the appeals and taking necessary measures to address the concerns.

item.title: Tajik and Russian Presidents Discuss Labor Migration, Regional Security, and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Presidents Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan and Vladimir Putin of Russia held talks in Dushanbe, focusing on labor migration, regional security, and economic ties. They discussed cooperation in energy, industry, mining, agriculture, and transport, as well as investments and joint work in AI and cybersecurity. Both leaders emphasized the importance of addressing labor migration issues.

item.title: Kazakhstan Explains 1.5 Billion Tenge Cost Difference in School Construction
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Education explained a 1.5 billion tenge cost difference between two schools built under the "Keleshek Mektepteri" national project. Factors cited include differing seismic activity and geological conditions, with one school requiring additional structural reinforcement due to its hillside location.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Tokayev Declares Attacking State Treasury a Heinous Crime
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that attacking the state treasury and violating constitutional norms are heinous crimes against the state. Speaking at the third Forum of Agricultural Workers, he emphasized a resolute fight against corruption and all societal vices, stressing that current performance, not past achievements, determines competence.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Investigate Coal Suppliers for Unjustified Price Increases
item.description: Uzbekistan's Antimonopoly Committee will investigate the justification of coal prices sold to the public and state organizations. Special attention will be paid to potential price gouging and unjustified markups by suppliers. The committee will also monitor economic concentration in the coal market.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Quality of Life Should Not Depend on Officials' Favor, Says President Tokayev
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that the quality of life for Kazakh citizens should not depend on the goodwill of officials, but on objective criteria like hard work and talent. He emphasized that responsible work and adherence to the 'Law and Order' principle are essential for all public servants and patriots.

item.title: Kazakhstan Health Ministry Official Discusses Antibiotic Resistance
item.description: Gulnara Kulkayeva, head of Kazakhstan's National Center for Public Health, spoke at a conference on antimicrobial resistance. She emphasized the need for rational antibiotic use to combat growing bacterial resistance. The conference, held at Nazarbayev University, gathered doctors, veterinarians, and scientists to discuss the 'One Health' approach to this global challenge.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Orders Review of Rural Support Programs
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed the government to conduct an analysis of the effectiveness of programs aimed at supporting rural areas. This directive signifies a focus on evaluating and potentially improving initiatives designed to bolster the agricultural sector and rural development across the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Economy Attracts Foreign Investment Across Multiple Sectors
item.description: As of November 1, Uzbekistan hosts 23,501 enterprises with foreign capital, actively participating in various economic sectors. Trade leads with 8,473 enterprises, followed by industry (4,493), information and communication (1,991), and construction (1,955). Favorable conditions continue to attract foreign investment.

item.title: Khorezm Region Criticizes Youth Employment Efforts, Plans Targeted Solutions
item.description: A meeting in Khorezm region reviewed youth employment and poverty reduction, criticizing the current approach. Plans include employing 7,411 school leavers, 3,305 vocational graduates, and 2,733 university graduates. Authorities were tasked with studying individual unemployment issues for targeted job placement.

item.title: Uzbek President's Role in Central Asian Cooperation Highlighted
item.description: At a meeting in Avaza, leaders of CIS parliaments met with Turkmenistan's National Leader Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow. The growing role of the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly in strengthening interstate relations and parliamentary dialogue was noted. Berdimuhamedow praised relations between Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan, highlighting President Mirziyoyev's leading role in regional cooperation.
